ns1:channel.ns1:title: Communications Earth & Environment
ns1:channel.ns1:description:
Communications Earth & Environment is an open access journal from Nature Portfolio that publishes high-quality research, reviews and commentary in the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. The papers we publish represent significant advances that bring new insight to a specialized area of research. We also provide a community forum for issues of importance to Earth, environmental and planetary scientists, regardless of sub-discipline.

Our scope covers all areas of the geosciences, climate and environmental sciences as well as planetary sciences, including those at the interface with ecology, sustainability and environmental social sciences. Primary research of interest to the journal includes important insights gained from field work, novel analyses of existing data, numerical or analytical modelling, theoretical studies or laboratory experiments.

We encourage submissions that provide independent confirmation of particularly influential publications.

The submission and review processes are managed by our in-house professional editors supported by our Editorial Board Members, who provide technical expertise across the breadth of the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. We are committed to rapid dissemination of important research results. Articles are published on a continuous basis to ensure swift communication of findings.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Pollution-driven surface water quality improvement and expanding population benefits in karst regions of China
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04006-9

Surface water quality in China’s karst regions improved substantially, with top-quality waters increasing by up to 36 percent and 4.86 million people benefiting, but gains may reverse without continued controls, according to remote sensing and machine learning.
ns1:item.dc:title: Pollution-driven surface water quality improvement and expanding population benefits in karst regions of China

ns1:item.ns1:title: Super micron Amazonian aerosol particles as efficient catalyzers at cirrus temperatures
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04019-4

Aerosol particles over north western Amazonia have ice nucleating abilities, according to analyses of aerosol data from a measurement site in Colombia.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Current model capabilities and future predictive pathways of wildfires under a changing climate
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04013-w

Modelling future wildfires across the world is highly uncertain despite improvements in fire-process representation and the introduction of hybrid frameworks integrating observations, process-based modelling, and machine learning.
ns1:item.dc:title: Current model capabilities and future predictive pathways of wildfires under a changing climate

ns1:item.ns1:title: Global drought shows no detectable recent acceleration under climate warming
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03954-6

No statistically significant acceleration in drought is detected across ~99% of quasi-global land area, according to a study that applied multiple Penman-type and energy-based potential evapotranspiration formulations to Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index records from 1981–2024.
